column1: # Phase E: name <TAB> SQE SQL <TAB> Snowflake SQL ("=" when identical). @S@ is the schema.
# Snowflake names are upper case and SQE quotes them; SQE names are lower case and Snowflake quotes them.
# Timestamps compare as epoch micros (nanos for the _NS table). Snowflake arrays are 0-based, SQE's 1-based.
# ST_AREA on a GEOMETRY Snowflake reads from an Iceberg table comes back negative, whichever
# engine wrote it (-12 for the same ring that gives 12 as a literal), so the Snowflake side takes ABS.
# Every Snowflake expression column is aliased: snow's JSON output keys rows by column name.

column2: SELECT "ID", "NAME", "AMOUNT", CAST("TS" AS BIGINT), CAST("NTZ" AS BIGINT), CAST("D" AS VARCHAR), "FLAG", "BIG", "DBL", upper(encode("BIN", 'hex')), CAST("T" AS BIGINT) FROM @S@."SF_RUN_BASIC" ORDER BY "ID"
column3: SELECT ID, NAME, AMOUNT, DATE_PART(epoch_microsecond, TS) AS TS_US, DATE_PART(epoch_microsecond, NTZ) AS NTZ_US, TO_VARCHAR(D, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS D_S, FLAG, BIG, DBL, HEX_ENCODE(BIN) AS BIN_HEX, DATEDIFF(microsecond, '00:00:00'::TIME, T) AS T_US FROM @S@.SF_RUN_BASIC ORDER BY ID

column2: SELECT "ID" FROM @S@."SF_RUN_BASIC" WHERE "TS" > TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00+00:00' ORDER BY "ID"
column3: SELECT ID FROM @S@.SF_RUN_BASIC WHERE TS > '2026-01-01 00:00:00 +00:00'::TIMESTAMP_LTZ ORDER BY ID

column2: SELECT "ID" FROM @S@."SF_RUN_BASIC" WHERE "NTZ" < TIMESTAMP '2000-01-01 00:00:00' ORDER BY "ID"
column3: SELECT ID FROM @S@.SF_RUN_BASIC WHERE NTZ < '2000-01-01 00:00:00'::TIMESTAMP_NTZ ORDER BY ID

column2: SELECT count(*), sum("AMOUNT"), CAST(min("D") AS VARCHAR), max("BIG") FROM @S@."SF_RUN_BASIC"
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) AS N, SUM(AMOUNT) AS S, TO_VARCHAR(MIN(D), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS MIN_D, MAX(BIG) AS MAX_BIG FROM @S@.SF_RUN_BASIC

column2: SELECT "ID", CAST("NS" AS BIGINT), CAST("TZNS" AS BIGINT) FROM @S@."SF_RUN_NS" ORDER BY "ID"
column3: SELECT ID, DATE_PART(epoch_nanosecond, NS) AS NS_NS, DATE_PART(epoch_nanosecond, TZNS) AS TZNS_NS FROM @S@.SF_RUN_NS ORDER BY ID

column2: SELECT "ID", "S".a, "S".b, "ARR"[1], "ARR"[3], cardinality("ARR"), "M"['k'], "M"['j'], cardinality("M"), "ARR_S"[1].x FROM @S@."SF_RUN_NESTED" ORDER BY "ID"
column3: SELECT ID, S:a AS SA, S:b AS SB, ARR[0] AS A0, ARR[2] AS A2, ARRAY_SIZE(ARR) AS NA, M['k'] AS MK, M['j'] AS MJ, MAP_SIZE(M) AS NM, ARR_S[0]:x AS AX FROM @S@.SF_RUN_NESTED ORDER BY ID
